quirks: Numeric readings are serialised as strings, so a value comparison is a string comparison unless the consumer casts.
Missing readings are the sentinel -999999, and variable.noDataValue states it. Treating the sentinel as a measurement produces a large negative discharge.
Provisional data carry the P qualifier and USGS revises them without notice; the provisional disclaimer is carried in the response's own queryInfo note block.
The JSON is a JAXB serialisation of WaterML, so the payload carries Java type wrappers (declaredType, globalScope) that are noise rather than data.
dateTime is local to the gage with an offset, not UTC. Comparing two gages without normalising compares two clocks.

conditions: Public domain covers USGS-authored material only. The instantaneous values service is USGS-authored; the clearance does not extend to third-party imagery elsewhere on usgs.gov.

declared_incentive.notes: The numbers are reported by the countries they describe, and headline aggregates carry political weight at home and consequences in negotiation. The World Bank harmonises but does not independently measure. Declared so that a revision to a back year is read as what it is, a restatement by the reporting country, rather than as an error by the publisher.

declared_lineage.notes: The World Bank compiles indicators from national statistical offices and other international agencies and harmonises them. Every figure here originates with a member country, which is why the incentive below sits with the country rather than with the Bank, and why a disagreement with a national source is expected rather than alarming.

denominator.notes: Population is published by the same API as SP.POP.TOTL for the same countries and years, so per-capita figures are computable within one source rather than assembled across two with mismatched vintages. Declared present on that basis; adding the population indicator as a second endpoint is the work that makes it usable.

records.notes: The response is a two-element array: a paging wrapper first, the observations second. The records therefore live at index 1, and the wrapper at index 0 carries lastupdated, which moves when the World Bank republishes and is counted as a metadata-change. date is the reference year and is the only identity an observation has. Revisions here are inferred from the value, because the API exposes no per-observation revision marker even though back years are restated routinely.

sources.name: World Bank Indicators API
quirks: The response is an array whose first element is the paging wrapper and whose second is the data; a client expecting an object gets nothing useful.
An error is returned as an array containing a message object with HTTP 200, so a failed query is a well-formed document.
date is the reference year as a string, and value is null for years a country did not report, which is different from zero and frequent.
Back years are restated without notice when a country revises its national accounts, and no field marks the restatement.
format=json must be passed explicitly; without it the API returns XML.

conditions: Credit must be given and changes indicated, including translations. The attribution string above satisfies this.
